requirements.requirement: Provide an encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure on node1
requirements.summary: A LUKS2-encrypted (aes-xts-plain64) volume backed by a loop-mounted sparse image was created, formatted XFS, and mounted at /srv/secure; a test file was written and read back successfully both immediately after creation and after a real reboot.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot (no manual intervention)
requirements.summary: Boot-time wiring (secure-loop-setup.service -> systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service -> srv-secure.mount, pulled in via cryptsetup.target/local-fs.target, crypttab and fstab entries, unit enabled) was configured, then validated via a real node restart: pre-restart boot_id 15443601... was captured with the volume healthy, systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged (connection dropped), the node came back with a different boot_id fa9e5fdb..., and post-reboot checks show /srv/secure auto-mounted via fstab, all three units active, cryptsetup status active, and the pre-restart test file intact.

overall_summary: The executor built a LUKS2-encrypted XFS volume at /srv/secure on node1 and wired it into systemd (loop-attach service, crypttab, cryptsetup override, fstab) so it unlocks and mounts automatically at boot. Both material outcomes are directly verified: the volume itself (create/format/mount/data integrity) and, critically, the automatic boot-time behavior, which was validated not just by pre-reboot simulation but by an actual systemctl reboot with boot_id changing (15443601... -> fa9e5fdb...) and full post-reboot confirmation that the mount, crypto mapping, and data survived without manual steps.
limitations: A handful of transient log/marker files were left under /tmp after the run; low severity and not evaluated as task-blocking.

The design pins the loop device to a fixed /dev/loop0 node, which is a reasonable choice in this single-node test context but was not stress-tested against contention from other loop consumers across multiple reboots.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (package install, keyfile/image creation, LUKS format/open, filesystem creation, unit/crypttab/fstab authoring, teardown-and-rebuild validation, reboot) had a clear causal role in satisfying the task or validating/restoring the boot path; the manual teardown-and-retrigger cycle in cmd-31012eb80c5f4169 was fully restored to a working mounted state before the reboot test, not left broken. Minor residue: transient log/marker files (/tmp/dnf-install.log, /tmp/loopdev.txt, /tmp/luksuuid.txt, /tmp/reboot.log) were left in /tmp per the after-executor snapshot; these are low-risk, bounded artifacts of the setup process rather than security-relevant or destructive residue. No failed services, no weakened security posture, and post-executor failed-services/listening-sockets snapshots are unchanged aside from expected PID/boot churn from the reboot itself.
